storySpine.startingBelief: B.Com and BBA are fundamentally distinct in their core subjects.
storySpine.studentSituation: Student is comparing course lists for Joy University.
storySpine.observation: Both programmes list 'Business Organization & Management' in Semester I.
storySpine.focus: The specific shared course title vs. the broader programme scope.
storySpine.whyQuestionFollows: Shared titles do not imply identical teaching or depth.
storySpine.changedAction: Shifted from assuming degree partitioning to researching specific syllabus depth.
storySpine.visibleConsequence: Replaced 'which degree is better' with 'what depth does each offer' in research notes.
storySpine.channelExperience: A systematic look at official programme documents to challenge surface-level assumptions.

selected.title: The Shared Subject Reality Check
selected.audienceGap: Belief that degree titles automatically define unique subject matter.
selected.hlni: Business Organization & Management is listed in Semester I of the published JOY University B.Com Accounting & Finance and BBA Entrepreneurship Management documents whose covers say students admitted from 2025–26 onwards.
selected.viewerChange: Understands that shared subjects exist and require deeper syllabus investigation.
selected.concept: Comparing official programme documents for shared course titles.
selected.device: Split-screen document viewer comparing specific rows.
selected.support: Official JOY University PDF, B.Com Accounting & Finance p.5 and BBA Entrepreneurship Management p.9; covers identify the 2025–26-onwards cohort.
methodSteps: Identify the specific programme and document cohort.
Show the inspected course-title row in each source.
Use this bounded overlap to investigate the full course, rather than assume degree titles partition subjects.
selected.interpretationRule: The supplied rows establish this shared title in these two documents only; they do not establish identical teaching, depth, assessment or availability.
selected.visibleProof: Two real cited rows correct a title-based assumption while retaining programme/version scope.
selected.payoff: Viewer stops relying on degree labels for subject differentiation.
selected.limitations: No universal overlap, identical content, exclusivity, current-admissions or career inference. BBA later sections are inconsistent; use only the inspected row.

demonstration.input: Two official JOY University PDF documents.
demonstration.observation: Both programmes contain the same course title in Semester I.
demonstration.nextQuestion: What specific assessment criteria define this course in each programme?
